findings.issue_text: app/models/optimized_image.rb:145-151 — Ruby has no overloading, so `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` at 145 is silently replaced by `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` at 149 (dead code, "method redefined" warning) and every existing 5-arg caller such as Upload.create_for's `OptimizedImage.downsize(file.path, file.path, width, height, allow_animation: allow_animation)` for profile_background/card_background now raises `ArgumentError: wrong number of arguments (given 5, expected 3..4)`, breaking those upload types entirely (severity P1, confidence 75)

app/models/optimized_image.rb:149-155 — `downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts)` turns `dimensions` into a free-form string whose validity depends on which backend `optimize` dispatches to, and the controller's `"80%"` is passed verbatim into `resize_instructions_animated` as `--resize-fit 80%`, which gifsicle rejects (it only accepts `WxH`/`_`, percentages need `--scale`), so with `allow_animated_thumbnails` on every oversized animated GIF gets 5 failing gifsicle shell-outs, `downsize` returns false each time, and the untouched oversized file falls through to `Upload.create_for` (severity P1, confidence 75)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:64-70 — the loop keys on `tempfile.size` (Ruby `Tempfile#size` is `@tmpfile.size`, an fstat on the open fd) but `convert_with` finishes each pass with `ImageOptim.new.optimize_image!(to)`, which replaces the file at that path via temp-file+rename, so from the second iteration on the fd points at an unlinked stale inode: the loop never observes later shrinkage and burns all 5 attempts, and `Upload.create_for(current_user.id, tempfile, filename, tempfile.size, ...)` records `filesize` and `FastImage.new(file)` width/height from the stale inode while `File.open(file.path)` stores the bytes of a different image (severity P1, confidence 50)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails)` couples the content of the user's ORIGINAL upload to a thumbnail-only setting: with the default `allow_animated_thumbnails=false` the non-animated path runs `convert #{from}[0] ... #{to}` in place, which selects frame 0 and permanently flattens every oversized animated GIF to a single static frame before the original is ever stored (severity P2, confidence 75)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:64 — the guard `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)` includes `.svg`, but unlike `OptimizedImage.create_for` (which special-cases `extension =~ /\.svg$/i` with a plain copy) the new loop pushes oversized SVGs through `convert file.svg[0] -resize 80%\> file.svg`, rasterizing the vector source in place and writing ImageMagick's MSVG output over the user's file (severity P2, confidence 50)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66-69 — the `while attempt > 0 && tempfile.size > ...` loop discards `downsize`'s boolean sentinel (`return false if $?.exitstatus != 0`), so a deterministic failure (missing binary, unsupported format, bad geometry) is retried 5 identical times and then the oversized or partially-written file proceeds straight into `Upload.create_for`; there is no verification step between the in-place transform and persistence, so a `convert` that truncates the output mid-write yields a `tempfile.size` below the limit and a corrupt image gets persisted as a valid Upload (severity P2, confidence 50)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:65-68 — ADVISORY: each loop pass is a full `convert` plus a full `ImageOptim` worker chain (optipng/pngquant/jpegoptim...) on a multi-megabyte file, up to 5 times, executed inside the web process (`Scheduler::Defer.later` thread, or inline for API `synchronous`); computing the scale factor once from `sqrt(max_bytes / tempfile.size)` and optimizing once at the end makes `attempt`, the `while` loop and the blind `"80%"` heuristic (which after 5 passes still only reaches ~10% of the original pixel area, so a 10MB upload against a 512KB `max_image_size_kb` is rejected anyway) unnecessary (severity P2, confidence 75)

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — `var maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024; // 10MB` replaces `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` for BOTH `type` values, so the client gate for attachments no longer honours `max_attachment_size_kb` at all (a 9MB attachment with a 1MB admin limit passes the client check and is only stopped, if at all, server-side) and the `file_too_large` alert reports 10240KB while the server enforces a different number; the same magic constant is hand-duplicated at utilities.js:246 and uploads_controller.rb:55 with no site setting as source of truth, guaranteeing drift when nginx `client_max_body_size` or the server limit changes (severity P2, confidence 75)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:63-70 — ADVISORY: the downsizing policy lives in the controller instead of next to the existing in-place `OptimizedImage.resize`/`downsize` transforms in `Upload.create_for`, so every other producer of uploads (`Jobs::PullHotlinkedImages`, `UserAvatar.import_url_for_user`, import scripts, plugins calling `Upload.create_for`) still fails on oversized images; moving the loop into `Upload.create_for` deletes the controller block and covers all entry points with one implementation (severity P2, confidence 75)

app/models/optimized_image.rb:145 — `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` is immediately shadowed by the second `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` at line 149 (Ruby keeps the last definition), so the retained width/height overload is dead code and any pre-existing 4/5-positional-arg caller now binds `max_height` to `opts` and crashes in `optimize` on `!!opts[:allow_animation]` (TypeError on Integer) or raises ArgumentError for 5 args; the changed public API of `resize`/`downsize`/`optimize` and the deleted `OptimizedImage.dimensions` ship with zero spec changes in the diff (severity P1, confidence 100)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:64 — the new downsize branch `if tempfile && tempfile.size > 0 && SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb > 0 && FileHelper.is_image?(filename)` is a new controller code path (image over limit -> shrunk; image under limit -> untouched; non-image -> skipped; API url path) with no controller spec added or modified anywhere in `git diff HEAD~2..HEAD --stat` (only utilities.js, uploads_controller.rb, optimized_image.rb, task-001.md), so the feature's acceptance criteria ("large images are automatically reduced to allowed size") are unverified (severity P1, confidence 100)

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — `var maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024; // 10MB` replaces `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` for BOTH `type === 'image'` and `type === 'attachment'`, so the client no longer consults `max_attachment_size_kb` at all: a non-image attachment between `max_attachment_size_kb` (default 1024 KB) and 10240 KB is fully uploaded, then rejected server-side by the unchanged `Upload.create_for` attachment-size validator, after the client already told the user the limit is 10240 KB (severity P2, confidence 75)

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:184 — `bootbox.alert(I18n.t('post.errors.file_too_large', { max_size_kb: maxSizeKB }))` now interpolates the hardcoded 10240 into the unchanged `post.errors.file_too_large` string ("maximum size is %{max_size_kb}KB") for images, while the server still rejects any image that is not under `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb` after the 5 `"80%"` passes (SVG, failed convert, incompressible raster), so the user is told two contradictory limits and no locale string was added to explain that images are auto-downsized (severity P2, confidence 75)

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — the constant `10 * 1024` silently clamps every deployment: an admin who raised `max_image_size_kb` or `max_attachment_size_kb` above 10240 KB is now blocked client-side by a limit that exists in no site setting, and the diff adds no setting (e.g. `max_upload_size_kb`) nor updates the `max_image_size_kb` setting description whose meaning changed from "reject above" to "downsize to" (severity P2, confidence 50)

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:246 — the 413 handler `var maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024; // 10 MB` reports 10240 KB whenever the web server rejects the body, but the 413 is produced by nginx `client_max_body_size`, which is not coupled to this constant; on any deployment whose nginx limit is below 10m the message names a limit the user cannot actually reach, and the diff includes no nginx/Rack limit change to make 10m the real ceiling (severity P3, confidence 50)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55 — `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, "discourse-upload-#{type}")` caps the API url path at a constant 10 MB independent of `max_image_size_kb`/`max_attachment_size_kb`; a non-image url (attachment) is now downloaded up to 10 MB and then rejected by the attachment-size validator, and an image url whose site limit is above 10240 KB is truncated to nil by `FileHelper.download` with no error surfaced (`rescue nil`) (severity P3, confidence 75)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:64 — `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)` matches `.svg`, so an SVG over `max_image_size_kb` is fed to `convert #{from}[0] ... -resize 80%\> #{to}` with `to == from`, rasterizing/re-encoding the vector file in place; the sibling path in optimized_image.rb:45 `if extension =~ /\.svg$/i FileUtils.cp(original_path, temp_path)` explicitly guards SVG and that guard was not propagated to the new branch (severity P2, confidence 75)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails)` gates animation on a *thumbnail* setting (default false), and `downsize_instructions` reads `#{from}[0]`, so with the default setting an animated GIF (or multi-page TIFF) over the size limit is silently flattened to its first frame and the flattened file overwrites the user's original upload with no warning to the user (severity P2, confidence 100)

app/models/optimized_image.rb:137 — when `allow_animated_thumbnails` is true, `downsize_instructions_animated` delegates to `resize_instructions_animated` which emits `--resize-fit #{dimensions}` = `--resize-fit 80%`; gifsicle only accepts `WxH` integer dimension pairs, so the command exits non-zero, `convert_with` returns false, all 5 attempts fail identically, and every animated GIF over the limit is rejected instead of downsized (severity P2, confidence 75)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 — the loop `while attempt > 0 && tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` discards the boolean returned by `OptimizedImage.downsize` (false on non-zero exit or exception), so a failing convert is retried 4 more identical times and then execution falls through to `Upload.create_for` with the still-oversized (or partially written, since `to == from`) file, and the user receives the generic size error with no indication downsizing was attempted (severity P2, confidence 75)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 — after the 5th pass (0.8^5 = 33% linear, ~11% of pixels) an image that is still above `max_image_size_kb` is handed to `Upload.create_for(current_user.id, tempfile, filename, tempfile.size, ...)` and rejected; nothing in the diff defines the acceptance criterion for "cannot be reduced enough" (no cap on passes relative to limit ratio, no distinct error, no log line), so a user who uploads e.g. a 9 MB PNG screenshot under the default 3072 KB limit sees only the old rejection message (severity P3, confidence 75)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 — `tempfile.size` on an open Rack `Tempfile` is an fstat of the already-open descriptor, while `convert` and `ImageOptim.new.optimize_image!(to)` rewrite the file by path; when image_optim replaces the file via rename (new inode) the descriptor keeps pointing at the pre-optimization bytes, so `tempfile.size` and the `file.read` used by the store see different content than `Digest::SHA1.file(path)` in `Upload.create_for`, producing a recorded sha1/filesize that do not match the stored bytes (severity P2, confidence 50)

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — ADVISORY: the existing QUnit coverage for `validateUploadedFile` sets `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb` and asserts rejection of a file above it; the diff changes the function to ignore that setting but touches no test under test/javascripts, so either that test now fails or no test exercises the new 10240 KB constant (severity P2, confidence 50)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)` rewrites the user's original bytes in place BEFORE `Upload.create_for` computes `sha1`/`width`/`height`, so the persisted Upload row describes only the lossy 80%-per-pass derivative, the original is discarded with no backup, no column/flag records that a downsize happened, and there is no rollback path for any upload created after this ships (severity P1, confidence 75)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 — the loop guard `while attempt > 0 && tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` reads `Tempfile#size` via fstat on the still-open fd, but `convert_with` ends with `ImageOptim.new.optimize_image!(to)` which replaces `tempfile.path` by rename (new inode), so after the first pass `tempfile.size` is frozen at the pre-optimization size, the condition never turns false, all 5 passes run (0.8^5 = 33% linear, ~11% of original pixels) even when pass 1 already satisfied the limit (verified locally: after rename-over, `t.size` stays 600 while `File.size(t.path)` is 100 and further in-place rewrites do not update it) (severity P1, confidence 75)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:72 — `Upload.create_for(current_user.id, tempfile, filename, tempfile.size, ...)` persists `filesize` from the orphaned old inode (fd-based `Tempfile#size`) while `Digest::SHA1.file(file)` reopens by path and hashes the new inode, so for every downsized upload the stored `filesize` column does not match the bytes the stored `sha1` identifies, and any consumer that reads the Tempfile through the fd (`FastImage.new(file)`, `file.read`) sees the pre-optimization bytes rather than the file at `tempfile.path` (severity P1, confidence 75)

app/models/optimized_image.rb:129 — `downsize_instructions` emits `#{from}[0]`, and with `allow_animated_thumbnails` at its default (false) the controller's `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails)` writes only frame 0 of an oversize animated GIF back over the original, so every frame after the first is irreversibly destroyed in the stored Upload and the user's animation is silently persisted as a static image (severity P1, confidence 75)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:64 — the gate `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)` admits `.svg`, yet the codebase already knows SVG must not be fed to convert (app/models/optimized_image.rb:45 `if extension =~ /\.svg$/i` copies instead of resizing), so an SVG larger than `max_image_size_kb` is run through `convert in.svg[0] -resize 80%\> in.svg` and the vector markup is overwritten with ImageMagick's SVG-writer output (rasterized/traced), destroying the original vector content in place with no recovery (severity P1, confidence 75)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — the boolean returned by `OptimizedImage.downsize(...)` is discarded; `convert_with` returns false both when `convert` exits non-zero after truncating the output (`from == to`, output opened "wb" before write, e.g. ENOSPC leaves a partial file) and when `ImageOptim.new.optimize_image!(to)` raises after convert already rewrote the file, so a failed transformation is indistinguishable from success and whatever bytes remain on disk are persisted verbatim by `Upload.create_for(..., tempfile.size, ...)` as the permanent Upload with `sha1`/`filesize` computed from the damaged file (the `tempfile.size > 0` guard runs once, before the loop) (severity P2, confidence 75)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:72 — the `sha1` persisted by `Upload.create_for` is now the hash of transformed bytes whose content depends on `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb` at upload time, the number of loop passes, and the installed ImageMagick/image_optim versions, so the same source image uploaded twice (after a setting change, on a different app server, or via a path that does not pass through this controller) produces different sha1 values, `Upload.find_by(sha1: sha1)` dedup misses, and duplicate Upload rows plus duplicate stored files accumulate for one original (severity P2, confidence 75)

app/models/optimized_image.rb:164 — ADVISORY: `ImageOptim.new.optimize_image!(to)` is now applied to the user's ORIGINAL upload (not a derived thumbnail) and image_optim's JPEG workers default to `jpegoptim --strip-all` / `jpegtran -copy none`, which strip the EXIF Orientation tag and ICC profile, so oversize phone photos are persisted rotated and colour-shifted relative to what the user uploaded; who gets bitten: anyone uploading a >max_image_size_kb camera JPEG; rebuttal gate: this is not a defect if `Upload.create_for` applies `-auto-orient` to the file BEFORE this point or ImageOptim is configured with strip disabled, neither of which is visible in this snapshot (severity P2, confidence 50)

app/models/optimized_image.rb:120 — ADVISORY: when `allow_animated_thumbnails` is enabled the `.gif` branch builds `gifsicle ... --resize-fit 80%`, and gifsicle's `--resize-fit` accepts only `WxH`/`_xH`/`Wx_` geometry, not a percentage, so gifsicle exits non-zero without touching the file, all 5 attempts spin, and the still-oversize GIF is handed to `Upload.create_for` unchanged; who gets bitten: sites with animated thumbnails on that expect large GIFs to be auto-reduced (no data loss, the feature is a no-op and the upload is rejected downstream); rebuttal gate: invalid if this gifsicle build accepts percentage geometry for `--resize-fit` (severity P2, confidence 50)

app/models/optimized_image.rb:149 — Ruby has no overloading, so `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` silently replaces the retained `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` at :145 (now dead code), and every pre-existing caller that still passes width and height as separate positional args (the reason the 5-arg def was kept) raises `ArgumentError: wrong number of arguments (5 for 3..4)` — or, with 4 args, gets the height Integer bound to `opts` and dies on `opts[:allow_animation]` — breaking those upload paths (severity P1, confidence 75)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 — `while attempt > 0 && tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` reads `Tempfile#size` via fstat on the open fd, but `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...)` ends in `ImageOptim.new.optimize_image!(to)` which renames its optimized temp copy over `to`, so after the first iteration the fd points at an unlinked stale inode: the loop condition is frozen at the first unoptimized convert output size, all 5 attempts run unconditionally (shrinking to 0.8^5 = 33% linear) whenever that stale size exceeds the limit, and the stale value is then handed to `Upload.create_for(current_user.id, tempfile, filename, tempfile.size, ...)` as `filesize` while any fd-based read in create_for (e.g. `FastImage.new(file)`) sees pre-downsize bytes (severity P1, confidence 75)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — with `allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails` true and a `.gif` tempfile, `optimize` dispatches to `downsize_instructions_animated` -> `gifsicle ... --resize-fit 80% ...`, and gifsicle's `--resize-fit` only accepts `WxH` (percent scaling is `--scale`), so gifsicle exits non-zero, `convert_with` returns false with no log line, the loop spins 5 times as a no-op, and oversized animated GIFs are never downsized (severity P2, confidence 75)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — with `allow_animated_thumbnails` false (the default) an oversized animated GIF is run through `downsize_instructions` as `convert #{from}[0] ... -resize 80%\> #{to}` with `from == to == tempfile.path`, so the `[0]` frame selector rewrites the user's ORIGINAL upload in place as a single static frame; the setting governs thumbnails, not originals, and the animation is destroyed before `Upload.create_for` ever sees it (severity P1, confidence 75)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:64 — the guard `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)` matches `.svg`, so an oversized SVG is fed to `convert big.svg[0] ... -resize 80%\> big.svg`; ImageMagick cannot vector-resize an SVG and its SVG writer either fails (loop no-ops, nothing downsized) or emits a rasterized per-pixel trace far larger than the input, whereas `OptimizedImage.create_for` at :45 already special-cases `extension =~ /\.svg$/i` to keep SVGs away from `convert` (severity P2, confidence 50)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 — the loop guard `while attempt > 0 && tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` reads `Tempfile#size` via fstat on the Tempfile's open fd, but `OptimizedImage.downsize` ends with `ImageOptim.new.optimize_image!(to)` whose `ImagePath#replace` does `temp.rename(src.to_s)` (new inode over the path), so after the first successful iteration the fd points at the unlinked pre-optim inode and `tempfile.size` is frozen at iteration-1's size: iterations 2-5 shrink the on-disk file but the guard never observes it, the loop always burns all 5 convert+optim rounds, and then `Upload.create_for(current_user.id, tempfile, filename, tempfile.size, ...)` passes the stale iteration-1 size to `UploadValidator` (`upload.filesize > max_size_bytes`) which rejects with "too big (maximum size is 3072KB)" even though the file on disk is now under the limit — any image whose single 80% pass is not enough (roughly >1.5x the limit, i.e. most of the newly-allowed 5-10MB range) is rejected after ~5 rounds of full-size ImageMagick work (severity P1, confidence 75)
